title: CF Meet enterprise calling bodies v1
description: Request and response bodies of Calling's enterprise calling API (Part F sections 52-62): the typed enterprise call policy, departments, extensions, ring groups, call queues, IVR flows, business hours, forwarding rules, voicemail mailboxes and messages, call-recording policies and recordings, administrative audit and the enterprise call context. Scope (tenant, application, environment) comes only from the authenticated credential and is never a body field. Mutations of existing resources carry expectedVersion. No body carries a raw telephone number (public forwarding targets are opaque ContactReferences), a provider, SIP or edge identifier, a DTMF digit sequence, an object-storage key or a public media URL. The root accepts exactly one of the bodies (fixtures); the HTTP contract references the $defs.

ResourceStatus.description: Lifecycle of an enterprise configuration resource. Configuration is never deleted: DISABLED stops future routing and keeps historical Call references valid.

AdminCapability.description: Organization-level administrative capabilities (second key after the credential's enterprise scopes). MANAGE_PUBLIC_FORWARDING and MANAGE_RECORDING are granted by a CF Meet operator only.

SpendPolicy.description: Where public-network spend of enterprise calls is accounted: the application's Part E telecom spend limits (one spend authority, referenced — never duplicated).

PolicyRules.description: The typed enterprise call policy (§18). Every hook is a typed field; unknown fields are refused. publicForwardingAllowed requires forwardingAllowed and externalPublicCallingAllowed; public effects still pass every Part E gate (routing policy, live telecom, ContactReference verification, destination country, spend, Privacy Relay, Telephony route).

BuiltinPrompt.description: The controlled built-in prompt catalog. The media plane plays its own copy (Telephony maps it to edge-local audio; an application client to its own asset). Never a URL, path, file name or synthesized text. Each prompt has a nominal length the media plane's audio must fit (WELCOME, MENU, NO_INPUT, GOODBYE 2 s; PLEASE_HOLD, TRANSFERRING, CLOSED 3 s; INVALID_OPTION 4 s; VOICEMAIL_GREETING 6 s; BEEP 1 s): a menu's input timer starts after the prompts it queued, and a HANGUP node's prompt plays for its nominal length before the platform ends the Call.
